name: Buff-bellied Puffbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Uncommon chunky pied species, usually noticed perched motionless in the canopy of humid and lower montane forests. Note its sturdy bill, narrow white forehead, white breast with a narrow black collar, and buffy belly.

name: Mangrove Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Coastal eastern australia (central queensland to hastings river, new south wales)
description: Medium-sized honeyeater found in coastal habitats of eastern Australia. Back is brown-green, breast is gray, and underparts are pale.

name: Blue-eared Lory
rangeDescription: Montane forest of seram (southern moluccas)
description: A spectacular, long-tailed bright red parrot with purple-blue cheeks and throat, scattered blue markings on the wings, and a deep blue belly. Juveniles duller, showing less blue.

name: Chestnut-headed Nunlet
rangeDescription: Northwestern brazil north of the amazon river and west of rio negro
description: Small puffbird with a large head and bill. Uncommon and rarely encountered, restricted to a small area along the Amazon river in central-western Amazonia.

name: White-tailed Emerald
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southern costa rica to central panama
description: Small hummingbird with restricted range in Costa Rica and western Panama. Male is mostly glittering emerald with a bright white lower belly and outer tail feathers.

name: Nelicourvi Weaver
rangeDescription: Evergreen mossy forest of northern, eastern, and southern madagascar
description: Dark olive-green forest-dwelling weaver. Male has a black cap and yellow collar; female plainer.

name: Patagonian Canastero
rangeDescription: Southern argentina (mendoza southward to northern santa cruz)
description: Drab canastero of central Argentina’s Monte desert region and northern Patagonian scrublands. Plain grayish-brown plumage and concolor tail distinctive in range.

name: Secretarybird
rangeDescription: Savanna and grassland of sub-saharan africa
description: A distinctive, tall, long-legged, crane-like raptor with unique quill-like plumes on its head and bright-red facial skin. In flight, the dark edge to the hind wing, diamond-shaped tail, and long spatulate tail feathers make it unmistakable.

name: Golden-backed Mountain Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (eastern la libertad to san martín and huánuco)
description: One of Peru’s most spectacular birds, rarely seen due to its remote and difficult-to-access habitat. It is only found in wet high-elevation forest near treeline in the eastern Andes of northern and central Peru.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Stripe-breasted Seedeater
rangeDescription: Eastern and southeastern south sudan, ethiopia, and western and central kenya
description: Medium-sized brown, heavily streaked seedeater. Note the streaked underparts and boldly marked face with a streaked crown, white eyebrow, and broad dark brown patch through the eye.

name: Marañon Spinetail
rangeDescription: Southern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) to northwestern peru (northern cajamarca)
description: Very shy spinetail restricted to the Marañon Valley of northwestern Peru and extreme southern Ecuador; highly threatened due to ongoing habitat loss. Plumage is mostly gray with chestnut back, wings, and tail.

name: Guadalupe Murrelet
rangeDescription: San benito island and guadalupe island (off baja california)
description: Small black-and-white diving seabird, unlikely to be seen from land. Usually found as singles or pairs, well offshore, and not usually associating with other seabirds.

name: White-tailed Blue Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Angola to southwestern uganda, tanzania, and northern mozambique
description: Slim, slightly crested flycatcher with a long tail that is often fanned. The back is blue, the underparts pale gray, and the outer tail white.

name: Indigo Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Andes of western colombia and northwestern ecuador (southward to pichincha)
description: Small flowerpiercer with restricted range in western Colombia and northwest Ecuador. Entirely ultramarine blue, though can appear dark in poor light.

name: Masked Crimson Tanager
rangeDescription: Humid southeastern colombia to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Small, attractive tanager; bright crimson and black with a black mask and silver bill. Most commonly found in vegetation around oxbow lakes, also sometimes found in nearby forests and along rivers.

name: Great Shearwater
rangeDescription: Islands in south atlantic ocean; ranges north atlantic to arctic circle
description: Large shearwater with a crisp dark cap. Long, narrow wings are held quite straight when flying; wingbeats are stiff.

name: Madagascar Snipe
rangeDescription: Marshes of eastern and central massif of madagascar
description: Chunky, cryptic, short-legged, long-billed shorebird. Found in thickly vegetated wetlands, including rice fields, in eastern and central Madagascar.

name: Malabar Woodshrike
rangeDescription: Southwestern india (western ghats from narbada river to kerala)
description: Large, dark woodshrike with ashy gray upperparts and darker gray wing panel and tail with a variable brownish tinge. A prominent black face mask surrounds the pale yellow iris.

name: Malaita Monarch
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A small black-and-white monarch. White below except for black throat and breast.

name: Semipalmated Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america; winters to southern south america
description: Small, grayish-brown sandpiper. Typically shows relatively short, blunt-tipped bill, but this varies across the breeding range: western populations are shortest-billed, eastern populations are longest, and females have longer bills than males!
